This is NOT the failed waist-grip pose: do not make a hand hold the staff at the belt and do not put the open empty hand in front. The front, screen-right hand GRIPS the staff firmly. The rear, screen-left hand is OPEN and EMPTY.
Pose planning in normalized canvas coordinates: Preserve Image 1 feet midpoint about (.37,.925), silver hair top about (.33,.19), head and lower body position, right-facing gaze and wide planted stance. Anatomical RIGHT shoulder is the near shoulder; right arm sweeps BACK/down to screen-left open hand near (.17,.56). Staff construction: ONE solid long crooked brown wooden staff matching the locked design, retaining the original length, thickness, distinctive ivory horned skull, turquoise spiral mark, suspended turquoise orb and feathers. Use a SINGLE continuous shaft, visible from the lower tail at about (.38,.78), diagonally up-right through the left hand grip (.64,.47), then through the wrapped upper wood to the crook at about (.84,.29). The skull is securely fastened to that upper crook near (.87,.35). The shaft centerline must stay aligned on both sides of the gripping fingers: fingers wrap and occlude a short grip segment, but wood visibly continues along the same diagonal above and below the fist. The lower shaft tail is visible beside the hip/thigh. Necklace: restore the original visible bone/tooth collar directly below the throat and above the dark bust garment. Several distinct small ivory teeth/fangs hang from a gold/ochre cord with the small teal center stone, as in Image 3. Readable pale ivory bones at the collar, not a gold-only necklace and not a skull attached to her neck. Preserve the waist skull ornament separately.
